The page introduces a category M with two hypotheses: every arrow is monomorphic, and every endomorphism of an object is the identity. A category defined by an ordered set is given as an example. The checks carry the two conditions as the page's hypotheses (007-HYPOTHESES); they do not certify an external example merely because it is named. The author's folio is 1 and the archival sheet number is 6. No date or separate manuscript title is recorded.

For D in M, the author defines the ordered collection of subobjects of D, written as a plain tilded D, and identifies D with its greatest element. The starred map sends u in Hom_M(D-prime,D) to its image subobject u(D-prime). The targeted check and separate re-proof of 007-INJECTIVE verify injectivity under the usual equivalence of monomorphisms: equality of the two subobjects gives a domain automorphism a with u=v a; hypothesis (ii) makes a the identity. Hypothesis (i) makes every displayed arrow a subobject representative.

The image is named Phi with lower D-prime and argument D; it consists of the subobjects Delta that are M-isomorphic to D-prime. The small M- is an insertion before isomorphes. The separate audit of 007-INJECTIVE also checks this image description: composing a subobject representative X to D with an isomorphism from D-prime to X gives an arrow with that same image subobject. The manuscript mapping has two rows, M below the final m of Hom, and an indented lower u with a longer arrow beginning farther left; these alignments are preserved without changing the mathematical letters.

The lower part introduces isomorphism classes of objects, first with a plain N and then with locally doubled N forms. The inserted sentence says “Il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii).”, with ordonné underlined. The checks of 007-CLASS-ORDER use the natural reachability relation on classes. Identities and composition give reflexivity and transitivity. Arrows in both directions compose to identities by (ii), so their objects are isomorphic and the classes coincide. That proves antisymmetry; (i) is not needed for this argument.

A representative D_n and its associated subobject order are described as determined or defined “à isom unique près”; the resulting family uses doubled J_n. The checks of 007-CANONICAL-TRANSPORT justify the canonical interpretation. If a and b are isomorphisms between the same two representatives, b-inverse composed with a is an endomorphism, hence the identity, so a=b. Composition with this unique M-isomorphism transports subobjects, respects their domain equivalence and factorization order, and has the inverse transport. The audit also verifies compatibility with identity and composition.

Uniqueness among all abstract order isomorphisms is a stronger statement, separately labeled 007-SUBOBJECT-ALL-ISOS, and is not attributed to the author's intended meaning. Its checked counterexample has objects A and B, two distinct arrows f,g from A to B, and only identity endomorphisms. All arrows are monic; the subobjects of B are two incomparable elements [f],[g] below [id_B]. Exchanging the first two gives a nonidentity order automorphism, whereas canonical transport induced by id_B is the identity. The checks use the text's set-level size convention; the two categorical hypotheses alone do not prove that all relevant classes and subobjects form sets.
